items.claim: Two prose facts in the Ammon row are untrue as written while its span holds. (1) Ezek.25.2 is presented as the book's first foreign addressee, but MT 21:33 (= WEB 21:28) already carries a messenger-formula oracle addressed "אֶל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן" (oshb:Ezek.21.33 = MT 21:33 = WEB 21:28), so an earlier foreign addressee stands in the book; the defensible fact is that Ezek.25.2 is the first foreign target of a set-your-face command (9-verse family: Ezek.6.2, Ezek.13.17, MT 21:2 (= WEB 20:46), MT 21:7 (= WEB 21:2), Ezek.25.2, Ezek.28.21, Ezek.29.2, Ezek.35.2, Ezek.38.2) and the first addressee of the whole nations collection. (2) Ezek.25.8 is labelled the row's forward hard seam, but Ezek.25.8 carries a messenger clause only: it is absent from the 39-verse strict and 41-verse any-form word-event lists and from the 14 year-bearing datelines, whereas the ruled hard-seam class is a dateline, a vision onset, or a word-event onset with a refrain or petuchah close behind it. The verified class for Ezek.25.8 is the addressee-change messenger cut.
items.both_sides: Onset side, Ezek.25.1 carries the strict 39-verse word-event onset and is also in the 41-verse any-form list, with no dateline term, and Ezek.25.2 adds the set-your-face command toward Ammon. Close side, the setumah the inventory records after Ezek.24.27 stands behind the row, and Ezek.25.7 closes on the 5-verse 2ms recognition refrain "אַשְׁמִ֣ידְךָ֔ וְיָדַעְתָּ֖ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" with a setumah after it. Both sides carry independent evidence, so the span and the row's handling of the earlier Ezek.25.5 close are sound; only the first-instance claim and the seam-class label fail.

items.claim: Two facts need correcting while the seam holds. (1) Ezek.26.1's dateline is called an explicit month-and-day dateline, but the verse names a year, "בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה", and a day of the month, "בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ" (oshb:Ezek.26.1), and carries no month ordinal at all; the contrast is Ezek.24.1, which does name one, "בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י" (oshb:Ezek.24.1). The true description is a year plus a day of the month, with the month unspecified. (2) The chapter's marked units are labelled four but enumerated as three ranges running to the chapter's end, which erases the setumah the inventory records after Ezek.26.18; the four marked closes are Ezek.26.6, Ezek.26.14, Ezek.26.18 and Ezek.26.21.
items.both_sides: Onset side, Ezek.26.1 is a dateline verse and a perfect-form word-event verse at once, which the ruled frame treats as a single dateline-grade onset that is never split, and it is in both the 14-verse dateline list and the 7-verse perfect-form list; behind it, Ezek.25.17 closed the four-nation set on the 3mp refrain with a setumah. Close side, Ezek.26.6 is in the 28-verse recognition list with a petuchah after it, and Ezek.26.7 reopens on a messenger clause against the same addressee, which is the ruled onset-and-close collision resolved at the verse boundary after the close verse. Both sides therefore support the span; what fails is the dateline's content and the unit enumeration.

suggested_fix.fact: Ezek.26.1 carries a year term and a day-of-the-month term with no month ordinal, so it is a year-plus-day dateline; and the chapter's marked closes number four, at Ezek.26.6, Ezek.26.14, Ezek.26.18 and Ezek.26.21.
